<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] attention: use FlashInfer SM90 DOTS3 MLA/SWA decode -->

## Motivation

Use FlashInfer's optimized Hopper implementation for DOTS3 sliding-window MLA
decode, now merged in [flashinfer#6823](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6823).
This replaces the existing composite fallback for supported inputs without
vendoring a kernel, adding a serving option, or changing other attention backends.

## Modifications

- Add a small adapter around the public FlashInfer
  `batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa` API and its workspace-size helper.
  Prepare reusable workspace and warm the module before CUDA Graph capture.
- Select the native path inside the existing DOTS SWA backend using actual
  **local SWA heads**, rather than full-attention heads. The qualified domain is:

  | Property | Native path |
  | --- | --- |
  | Hardware | SM90; at least 223,584 bytes of opt-in shared memory |
  | Data type | BF16 queries and KV cache |
  | Local batch | 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 |
  | Query length | 1 or 4; bounded decode, not general prefill |
  | Local query / KV heads | 64 / 1 |
  | QK / value dimension | 1088 / 1024 |
  | KV cache | Contiguous Page64 latent cache; no repacking |
  | Window | 513 tokens: current position plus up to 512 preceding keys |
  | Attention context parallelism | 1 |

- Keep the existing fallback for unsupported devices, shapes or layouts, and
  older FlashInfer installations without the optional API. For example,
  attention-TP8 with local SWA Hq=8 stays on fallback. Prefill, draft-model
  routing and other decode backends are unchanged.
- Include this adapter in the existing startup FlashInfer autotune context,
  including discovery through DOTS and two-batch-overlap backend wrappers.
- Do not suppress compilation, loader/ABI or CUDA execution errors. An explicit
  missing-AOT condition with JIT disabled may retain fallback.
- Add one CPU/H100-registered test file covering native execution, Graph replay,
  autotune, selection guards, optional-API fallback and error propagation.

No dependency pin change is included. Native execution requires a FlashInfer
build containing #6823; an older installation continues to work through fallback.
No additional environment variable or decode-backend argument is required.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated the submitted SGLang head `0dcac687` (based on main `52a6f704`)
against FlashInfer main `f810e74b`, which includes #6823. Environment:
NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 / 132 SMs, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0.

| Test | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh FlashInfer SM90 MLA/SWA JIT build and source-path verification | Passed |
| FlashInfer kernel and trace tests | 183 passed, no skips |
| SGLang adapter and existing DOTS backend tests | 21 passed, no skips |
| Direct invocation of the registered adapter test file | 15 passed |
| Existing upstream FlashInfer-autotune synchronization suite | 12 tests and 7 subtests passed |
| CPU-only adapter and DOTS tests | 18 passed, 3 expected GPU-only skips |
| Native adapter versus SGLang fallback, all 10 supported batch/query-length combinations | Passed |

Adapter coverage includes actual native execution, saved autotune-cache entries,
bitwise eager/Graph-replay agreement, unsupported-shape and missing-API fallback,
missing-AOT handling, and propagation of non-recoverable execution errors.

The 10-shape comparison explicitly requires native selection for local batch
1/2/4/8/16 and query length 1/4, with Hq=64, KV length=1055, Page64 and W513.
Relative L2 against the actual SGLang fallback is 0.00771–0.00874, below the
0.03 smoke-test threshold. This comparison is not a bitwise-identity claim:
the two implementations have different arithmetic paths. FlashInfer's kernel
tests independently check numerical references and masked NaN/Inf KV cases.

Reproduction, with the required dependencies and a FlashInfer build containing #6823:

```bash
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"

python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_swa.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_dots_hybrid_backend.py

python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py

# Registered-CI entrypoint; propagates pytest failures to the process exit code.
python test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_swa.py
```

These are operator/backend integration results, not model-quality qualification.
The earlier FlashInfer-path dummy-weight full-model eager test passed, but it
predates this rebase. Full-model CUDA Graph and real-weight qualification through
the new FlashInfer path remain deferred; this PR does not claim those as passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Complete attention-operation latency, **including any separate split combine**.
NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 / 132 SMs, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0;
BF16, local Hq=64, QK/V dimensions=1088/1024, KV length=4127 (Page64 offset31),
W513, scale=0.0625. Warm-cache CUDA Graph timing: 12 interleaved rounds,
300 replays per round; median latency in microseconds.

The baseline is SGLang's existing
`forward_dense_kvlora_swa_torch_fallback` (Torch BMM/softmax plus Triton
gather/masking), not another FlashInfer kernel. Global batch is the
attention-DP8 deployment mapping; each operator call uses the listed local batch.

| Query length | Global / local batch | Fallback (µs) | FlashInfer (µs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 8 / 1 | 19.278 | 11.548 | 1.669× |
| 1 | 16 / 2 | 20.105 | 14.410 | 1.395× |
| 1 | 32 / 4 | 23.147 | 17.233 | 1.343× |
| 1 | 64 / 8 | 25.923 | 24.959 | 1.039× |
| 1 | 128 / 16 | 38.873 | 26.982 | 1.441× |
| 4 | 8 / 1 | 21.228 | 16.923 | 1.254× |
| 4 | 16 / 2 | 22.762 | 24.394 | 0.933× |
| 4 | 32 / 4 | 27.060 | 25.506 | 1.061× |
| 4 | 64 / 8 | 36.891 | 33.380 | 1.105× |
| 4 | 128 / 16 | 62.907 | 51.569 | 1.220× |

Nine of ten shapes improve; local batch2/query length4 is about 7.2% slower.
The supported-shape guard is a correctness/support guard, not a guarantee of
winning against fallback in every shape.

These measurements were collected on 2026-10-21 using FlashInfer `139aec4d`
and the pre-rebase companion SGLang integration. They include the masked-KV
repair and required P async-proxy fences. The merged FlashInfer API, binding
and kernel sources used in the latest validation are byte-identical to that
measured version; SGLang's runtime integration patches survived rebase unchanged.
The latest SGLang rebase was revalidated for correctness, but this performance
table was **not rerun on that exact rebase**. These are operator measurements,
not full-model throughput or end-to-end speedups.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Changed-file repository hooks, including registered-test checks, passed without
rewriting the tested sources. No separate SGLang documentation page was added.
Operator accuracy/performance evidence is provided above; full-model
accuracy/throughput qualification on the submitted integration remains deferred,
so that broader checklist item is intentionally not marked complete.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+# Copyright 2026 SGLang Team
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Optional FlashInfer MLA+SWA decode; prefill and other backends are unchanged."""
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.swa_mla_fallback.forward import (
+    forward_dense_kvlora_swa_torch_fallback,
+)
+
+
+class FlashInferMLASWA:
+    """Own workspace for one serial attention backend, prepared before capture."""
+
+    def __init__(self, run, workspace):
+        self.run = run
+        self.workspace = workspace
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create(cls, device):
+        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            return None
+        device = torch.device(device)
+        if device.type != "cuda" or torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device) != (9, 0):
+            return None
+        props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device)
+        if props.shared_memory_per_block_optin < 223584:
+            return None
+        try:
+            import flashinfer.mla as mla
+        except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:
+            if exc.name in ("flashinfer", "flashinfer.mla"):
+                return None
+            raise
+        run = getattr(mla, "batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa", None)
+        size = getattr(mla, "get_mla_swa_workspace_size_bytes", None)
+        if run is None or size is None:
+            return None  # Older optional dependency, not a CUDA/ABI failure.
+        from flashinfer.jit import MissingJITCacheError
+
+        workspace = torch.empty(size(16, 4, 64), dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        # One real eager call populates module/device caches through the public
+        # API. No private wrapper, tensor-value D2H, or capture-time compilation.
+        q = torch.zeros((1, 1, 64, 1088), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        kv = torch.zeros((1, 64, 1088), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        table = torch.zeros((1, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        lengths = torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        try:
+            run(q, kv, workspace, table, lengths, window_left=512, sm_scale=0.0625)
+        except MissingJITCacheError:
+            # JIT explicitly disabled with no matching optional AOT artifact.
+            # Do not catch compiler, loader/ABI, or CUDA execution failures.
+            return None
+        return cls(run, workspace)
+
+    def supports(
+        self, q, kv, table, lengths, layer, kv_cache_dim, head_dim_v, window_size
+    ):
+        return (
+            q.is_cuda
+            and q.device == self.workspace.device
+            and kv.device == q.device
+            and table.device == q.device
+            and lengths.device == q.device
+            and q.ndim == 4
+            and q.shape[0] in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16)
+            and q.shape[1] in (1, 4)
+            and q.shape[2:] == (64, 1088)
+            and q.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+            and kv.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+            and q.stride()[-3:] == (64 * 1088, 1088, 1)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import sys
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.swa_mla import FlashInferMLASWA
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci, register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=12, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+def test_cpu_keeps_fallback():
+    assert FlashInferMLASWA.create("cpu") is None
+

+def test_older_flashinfer_keeps_fallback(monkeypatch):
+    import flashinfer.mla as mla
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_available", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "get_device_capability", lambda device: (9, 0))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        torch.cuda,
+        "get_device_properties",
+        lambda device: SimpleNamespace(shared_memory_per_block_optin=227328),
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mla, "batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa", None, raising=False)
+    assert FlashInferMLASWA.create("cuda:0") is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "heads,swa_heads,cp,expected",
+    [(128, 64, 1, True), (16, 8, 1, False), (128, 64, 2, False), (64, None, 1, False)],
+)
+def test_wrapper_prepares_only_qualified_domain(
+    monkeypatch, heads, swa_heads, cp, expected
+):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.attention.dots_hybrid_backend import DotsSWAMLAAttnBackend
+
+    marker = object()
+    calls = []
+
+    def create(device):
+        calls.append(device)
+        return marker
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(FlashInferMLASWA, "create", create)
+    inner = SimpleNamespace(
+        num_attention_heads=heads,
+        attn_cp_size=cp,
+        device="cuda:0",
+        token_to_kv_pool=object(),
+        req_to_token_pool=object(),
+        kv_index_translator=object(),
+    )
+    wrapper = DotsSWAMLAAttnBackend(inner, num_swa_heads=swa_heads)
+    assert (wrapper._mla_swa is marker) == expected
+    assert bool(calls) == expected
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("attn_tp_size,expected", [(1, 64), (8, 8)])

+def test_missing_aot_is_recoverable_but_other_errors_propagate(monkeypatch):
+    import flashinfer.mla as mla
+    from flashinfer.jit import MissingJITCacheError
+
+    if not hasattr(mla, "batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa"):
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer MLA+SWA API unavailable")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "is_available", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.cuda, "get_device_capability", lambda device: (9, 0))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        torch.cuda,
+        "get_device_properties",
+        lambda device: SimpleNamespace(shared_memory_per_block_optin=227328),
+    )
+    for name in ("empty", "zeros", "ones"):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(torch, name, lambda *args, **kwargs: object())
+
+    def missing(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise MissingJITCacheError("JIT disabled, artifact absent")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mla, "batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa", missing)
+    assert FlashInferMLASWA.create("cuda:0") is None
+
+    def broken(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise RuntimeError("loader or CUDA execution error")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(mla, "batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla_swa", broken)
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="execution error"):
+        FlashInferMLASWA.create("cuda:0")

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA required")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sq", [1, 4])
+def test_public_api_adapter_and_fallback(monkeypatch, tmp_path, sq):
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (9, 0):
+        pytest.skip("SM90 required")
+    adapter = FlashInferMLASWA.create(torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device()))
+    if adapter is None:
+        pytest.skip("FlashInfer MLA+SWA API unavailable")
+    import flashinfer
+
+    q = torch.randn(1, sq, 64, 1088, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kv = torch.randn(17 * 64, 1, 1088, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    table = torch.arange(17, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)[None]
+    lengths = torch.tensor([1055], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(tp_k_head_num=1, scaling=0.0625, is_cross_attention=False)
+    cache = tmp_path / "mla_swa.json"
+    with flashinfer.autotune(True, cache=str(cache)):
+        adapter.forward(q, kv, table, lengths, layer, 1088, 1024, 513)
+    assert cache.is_file()
+    assert "mla_swa_sm90" in cache.read_text()
+    expected = adapter.forward(q, kv, table, lengths, layer, 1088, 1024, 513)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual = adapter.forward(q, kv, table, lengths, layer, 1088, 1024, 513)
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    marker = torch.empty(0, device="cuda")
+    calls = []
+
+    def fallback(*args):
+        calls.append(args)
+        return marker
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "sglang.srt.layers.attention.swa_mla.forward_dense_kvlora_swa_torch_fallback",
+        fallback,
+    )
+    assert (
+        adapter.forward(q[:, :, :8], kv, table, lengths, layer, 1088, 1024, 513)
+        is marker
+    )
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+
+    def fail(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise RuntimeError("CUDA execution errors must propagate")
+
+    adapter.run = fail
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="must propagate"):
+        adapter.forward(q, kv, table, lengths, layer, 1088, 1024, 513)
+    assert len(calls) == 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))
